# 3 Maccabees Chapter 4 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Alexandrinus) | **Section:** The Jews Imprisoned in the Hippodrome

---

**1** Wherever this decree was announced, it was celebrated by the Gentiles as a festival, with joy and gladness, all the hatred they had long hidden finally breaking out in the open.

**2** But among the Jews there was unbroken mourning, lamentation, and weeping; their hearts burned with grief as they mourned over the sudden catastrophe that had overtaken them.

**3** What district, what city, what neighborhood, what street was not filled with weeping and lamentation over them?

**4** They were driven out with such bitter and merciless cruelty by the generals in every city that even some of their enemies were moved to pity at the sight of their extraordinary suffering. It made them reflect on the uncertainty of life, thinking that the same reversals could overtake themselves at any moment.

**5** A multitude of old men with white hair, bent from the rough treatment they had endured along the way, their legs bowed from age and shame, were driven along.

**6** Young women who had just entered the marriage chamber to share in the joy of wedded life, their faces veiled in grief rather than happiness, their fragrant ointments replaced by unwashed hair, were driven along; instead of wedding songs, they were escorted with laments.

**7** They were dragged forcibly in chains, in full public view.

**8** In public disgrace and wretched misery they were pushed onto ships and brought with their children to Alexandria.

**9** On their arrival there, the king ordered them gathered into the hippodrome in front of the city.

**10** The place was enormous and magnificently suited to such a purpose; it was positioned so that everyone entering or leaving the city, and everyone going to the royal palace, could see the Jews exposed there.

**11** This was done out of pure malice, so that the people who had already been stripped of everything would also be subjected to public humiliation.

**12** And there, imprisoned like condemned criminals awaiting death, the Jews waited.

**13** Ptolemy had instructed Hermon, the elephant keeper, to get his five hundred war elephants thoroughly drunk on undiluted wine mixed with frankincense and then release them against the Jews at dawn, so that they would be trampled underfoot.

**14** In this way all the Jews packed together in the hippodrome would be destroyed.

**15** But when the king had given these instructions, his friends who were present, appalled at his extreme and mindless cruelty toward the Jews, pleaded with him to rescind the order, saying:

**16** O king, do not do this! Do not bring ruin on your kingdom by dealing so brutally with people who have done nothing wrong.

**17** But the king flew into a rage and refused to listen.

**18** When morning came, however, the order had not been carried out, and the guards came to the king to report that the elephants had not been prepared.

**19** The king was furious and threatened Hermon and his men with severe punishment for the failure.

**20** But Hermon and his officers excused themselves, saying the elephants had not been given the wine in time.

**21** The king put off the punishment until the next day and issued the same order again.

**22** All that day, the assembled Jews in the hippodrome prayed to God with tears and lamentation.

**23** They called on the Almighty Lord, Master of all power, their merciful God and Father, begging him to turn aside the terrible plan being carried out against them.
